items.headline: Cisco's mail gateway can be rooted by one crafted email; found in a TAC support case, exploitation confirmed

immediate_action.action: A remote, unauthenticated attacker gains root on the appliance by sending it one crafted email; there is no workaround and no mitigation short of upgrading. Cisco found this in a TAC support case, and CISA lists it as exploited. Upgrade every physical and virtual Secure Email Gateway appliance today and hunt mail_logs for the pattern Cisco names before assuming a device is clean; a clean result does not rule out the S/MIME injection.
immediate_action.title: Patch every Cisco Secure Email Gateway now: unauthenticated root RCE via a single email, already exploited

items.summary: Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-76461 (CVSS 9.8) on 2026-09-14: an unauthenticated attacker who sends a single crafted email containing SQL statements to a Cisco Secure Email Gateway can execute arbitrary OS commands as root. Cisco confirms active exploitation and says the flaw was found during the resolution of a TAC support case; there is no workaround. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day. Cisco simultaneously shipped a hardening release fixing five further internally-found vulnerabilities in the same product; Cisco's hardening advisory says two vulnerabilities from its internal review are known to be exploited, this one and the arbitrary file write CVE-2026-76519. On 2026-10-31 Cisco re-released the 15.5.5-014 fix in light of new information related to exploit code available online, so a 15.5 appliance patched earlier needs a check of its Retro Remediation Engine version. Public Metasploit modules now exist for the exploited injection (merged 2026-11-05, its author's medium-confidence match to CVE-2026-76461) and for a second S/MIME injection that its author believes is CVE-2026-76443, for which Cisco names no fixed 16.0 build.

items.headline: Two exploited NetScaler zero-days: one in default configuration, one on by default on VPN servers; no workaround

immediate_action.action: Citrix confirms CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 are being exploited against unmitigated NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances right now, and Google's Mandiant reports exploitation since at least early September. CVE-2026-88771 requires no configuration at all: every default deployment is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker; CVE-2026-88772 is reachable wherever DTLS is enabled, which Citrix states is the default on any VPN virtual server. Citrix lists no workaround, and Mandiant's interim network controls (disable DTLS where it is not needed, block inbound UDP/443 upstream) cover CVE-2026-88772 only. Capture forensic evidence (logs, an instance snapshot where the appliance is virtual, a support bundle, a core dump) from each exposed appliance before patching, since the upgrade itself can destroy evidence of prior compromise, then upgrade to 14.1-73.37+ or 13.1-64.23+ (run `show ns variable` first on 13.1; if it returns any variables, install 13.1-64.24 instead to avoid a known reboot loop), going straight to 14.1-73.41+ or 13.1-64.28+ where the appliance is configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider (CVE-2026-88779), and to 14.1-73.46+ or 13.1-64.29+ where it is an identity provider (CVE-2026-107406), and run a compromise assessment on every appliance that was internet-facing.
immediate_action.title: Patch every internet-facing NetScaler ADC/Gateway now and check for pre-patch compromise

items.headline: Refrigeration attacks reach Switzerland, a Köniz butcher and three Volg stores; no actor established
items.summary: Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed to AFP a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of French stores; on 2026-11-02 more than 115 stores in at least six more countries and the first German shops followed. The French blood service EFS confirmed on 2026-11-03 that an incident at its refrigeration supplier altered the temperature and defrost thresholds of cold rooms at three EFS sites on 2 November, caught by its own alarms with no loss of blood products, and ENISA, the European Commission, Europol and the CSIRTs Network advised organisations on 2026-11-04 to take immediate action to mitigate exposure; no source ties the blood-service case to the Danfoss, Copeland or Dixell controllers. SRF reported on 2026-11-05 the first publicly known cases in Switzerland, a butcher in Köniz whose freezer reached 50 to 70 degrees and three Volg stores whose cooling parameters were changed; BACS has received one reportable notification, and CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA and DOT published a joint warning on refrigeration and cold-chain controllers that names no vendor. CERT-FR reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited and Coop Switzerland says attempts against it failed, ANSSI says elementary flaws were exploited, controllers directly on the internet and weak passwords, and SentinelLABS says responsibility has not been publicly established. Reuters and Nextgov report that the Pentagon treats freezer failures at US military commissaries as a suspected hack. NCSC Switzerland's advisory, updated on 2026-11-06, says the public information does not establish a common attack method or confirm exploitation of the Danfoss CVEs it lists, and Ransom-ISAC's log of one Copeland XWEB Pro compromise shows 743 parameter writes in two administrator sessions, with default credentials claimed.

items.headline: VulnCheck caught exploitation of the Node-RED flaw in Siemens IoT2050; all four variants affected, V4.3.4-1 fixes

actions: In every Entra tenant you run or manage for others, list the app registrations that hold client secrets, starting with multitenant, delegated-admin (GDAP) and Partner Center apps, security-tool integration apps and Azure DevOps service connections, and search the service-principal and non-interactive sign-in logs for the invalid-secret or expired-secret errors AADSTS7000215 and AADSTS7000222 followed by a success for the same app; on any hit remove all client secrets, certificates and federated credentials on that app, including ones you did not add, disable its service principal if needed and rotate everything stored in any Key Vault it could read, because issued tokens stay valid until they expire.
items.headline: Entra app-credential abuse: agents hunt GitHub for secrets, an operator reaches MSP clients, government among them
items.summary: Microsoft reports that since August threat actors have used the agentic framework ARTEX to query public GitHub for OAuth application secrets and cloud keys, and that from 2026-10-28 valid application credentials were used for service-principal sign-ins across dozens of applications in several tenants, a vendor-owned multitenant application among them. items.headline: Vaud: device-code phishing against Microsoft 365 is running in Romandie; several organisations already affected
items.summary: The canton of Vaud said on 2026-11-04 that a Microsoft 365 device-code phishing campaign is running in French-speaking Switzerland and that several organisations are already affected: mail that appears to come from a company or a known contact leads the reader to type a code on a genuine Microsoft sign-in page, which gives the attacker access to the account. If your organisation's pension administration, HR or payroll runs on PK Softech software, is being migrated to it or tested on it, or your staff are insured with Pensionskasse Post, ask the supplier or the fund in writing whether your data, test data included, was in the affected environment, project, test and migration copies included, and what it holds outside the productive system.
items.headline: PK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had promised in writing to delete; Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB
items.summary: PK Softech AG, the software supplier of Publica and other Swiss pension funds, says unknown attackers used malware to reach part of its IT and that data must be assumed to have left; the Confederation headlined its 2026-10-08 release "data outflow confirmed", and the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating. Tamedia reports that PK Softech had confirmed in writing in January 2026 that it deleted Publica's 2019 migration data, which apparently stayed on its servers, and that Akira holds about 100 GB and demands ransom; Inside IT relays this and adds that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira took data, and Netzwoche relays that the authorities assume data on practically all current and former federal and federally affiliated staff left. Publica says personal data of insured persons has presumably left; the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich says its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Pensionskasse Post says personal data left, the Bernische Pensionskasse says it must be assumed so, the Ticino fund IPCT says data of about 1,800 of its insured persons sat on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more, and other funds are still checking. The Federal Data Protection Commissioner, who opened a formal investigation against PK Softech on 2026-10-22, states that data of several pension funds, Publica among them, was exfiltrated. Publica's own newsletter of 2026-10-22 says the Akira group is being associated with the attack; the demand rests on the press reports. The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich has suspended its planned 2027 move to PK Softech's system, PK Softech cannot rule out that non-pseudonymised data was temporarily present in project work, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office has added the case to its criminal proceeding against Akira.

items.summary: GitLab's critical patch release of 2026-10-12 fixes CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS 3.1 10.0), an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular-expression compiler that lets code run on the server as the git user through a crafted expression in a CI/CD configuration. items.headline: VMware vCenter's pre-auth Syslog RCE is exploited; patch it with the auth bypass and VMXNET3 escape, no workaround
items.summary: Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0006 (2026-07-29) fixes five flaws across VMware ESX, vCenter, Workstation and Fusion, and NCSC-CH, NCSC-NL and BSI CERT-Bund all carried it across 2026-07-28 and 2026-07-29. CVE-2026-59309 (CVSS 9.8) is an authentication bypass in vCenter's Directory Service reachable with nothing but network access to vCenter, and CVE-2026-59310 (CVSS 9.8) is a directory traversal in vCenter's Syslog server that reaches arbitrary code execution. CVE-2026-47876 (CVSS 9.3) is an out-of-bounds write in the VMXNET3 virtual network adapter that lets a guest administrator execute code on the ESX host, affecting only VMs using that adapter. No workaround exists for any of the five, so patching is the only control. All were reported privately to Broadcom, one of them through Pwn2Own, and CVE-2026-59310 has since been exploited in the wild and was added to CISA's KEV catalog on 2026-08-18; CISA also listed the ESX logging flaw CVE-2026-41709 as exploited on 2026-10-28, the day CrowdStrike said the actor WARP PANDA used it as a zero-day.

items.headline: Microsoft patches an exploited Windows Shell zero-day that evades Mark of the Web protections on files and links
items.summary: Microsoft's 2026-10-13 updates fix CVE-2026-96951, a Windows Shell flaw that lets an attacker evade Mark of the Web defenses once a user opens a crafted file or link sent by email or instant message, so Windows does not show the dialog the tag normally triggers. Microsoft marks it exploited and CISA added it to KEV the same day; no source names the actor, the payload or the victims. Rapid7 says Windows Server 2012 gets no patch, while Microsoft lists fixes for Server 2012 R2 and every later supported release.

actions: Patch CVE-2026-46300 on every Linux host that runs PHP or other internet-facing code, then on multi-tenant hosts, container nodes and CI runners: apply the distribution kernel update and reboot; until then, where IPsec is not in use, block and unload the `esp4`, `esp6` and `rxrpc` modules (this breaks IPsec), and drop the page cache so a file already modified in memory reloads from disk.

On any PHP web host, appliance or management server that was reachable and unpatched for the PHP2Shell flaws, look for PHP files in web-reachable directories that nobody deployed, an outbound SSH session from the host that a systemd service or an rc.local entry keeps up, and password-spray bursts against Active Directory from the host's address, because Dream Research reports a chain of the two flaws that did exactly that.
items.headline: CVE-2026-46300 (Fragnesia): CISA lists the Linux kernel root flaw as exploited, chained with PHP2Shell
items.summary: CVE-2026-46300 ("Fragnesia", CVSS 7.8) is a local privilege escalation in the Linux kernel's xfrm ESP-in-TCP path, one of three CVEs Red Hat groups as "Dirty Frag"; CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 and says it can be chained with the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root, and Dream Research reports such a chain against 25 Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall and management servers and a US government-affiliated network. Its public exploit overwrites /usr/bin/su in the page cache, and Red Hat confirms RHEL kernels are affected (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28 · Dream Research, 2026-10-29 · Red Hat RHSB-2026-003).

items.headline: Balbooa Gridbox for Joomla: anonymous Super User flaws exploited since July; update to 2.20.4.2
items.summary: The mySites.guru research campaign against Joomla third-party extensions produced six further disclosures between 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-23, and one of them changes technique class: the Balbooa Gridbox page builder (CVE-2026-61425) trusts a client-supplied cookie value as proof of identity, so setting an administrator's username in that cookie authenticates the requester as that user with no password and no existing session. A Joomla Super User can edit templates, which is PHP execution, so this is full site compromise from a single anonymous request. Fixed in Gridbox 2.20.1; the researcher says the vulnerable code shipped for at least nine months. The same week added unauthenticated SQL injection and order-forgery flaws in EasyStore, an invoice IDOR in Events Booking, and a critical unauthenticated upload in Membership Pro. A follow-up audit of Gridbox produced eleven more CVEs, fixed in 2.20.2, four of them exploited in the wild, and Gridbox 2.20.3.1 (21 September) fixes a further unauthenticated SQL injection present in every earlier build. Gridbox 2.20.4.2 (27 October) fixes two more unauthenticated SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 and CVE-2026-102789, with no exploitation reported.

items.headline: PAN-OS management interfaces were rooted in the wild via PHP2Shell and a kernel flaw: hotfix, then check for compromise
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks' advisory, first published on 2026-10-21 and revised since, says active exploitation has been observed against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet, and Dream Research, with Unit 42's verification, reports a custom PHP2Shell build chained with a Linux kernel flaw that rooted 25 PAN-OS firewall and management servers in the United States, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea and went on to attack a US government-affiliated Active Directory. The advisory lists every release below the hotfix for its train, of PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1, 11.2, 11.1 and 10.2 and of Panorama, as affected through the management web interface by CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS-B 9.2); all twenty hotfixes are released, and GlobalProtect and the captive portal are not affected. A device that was exposed and unpatched needs a compromise check as well as the hotfix, and CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26.

items.headline: Cisco ASA and FTD SSL VPN reload flaw is exploited and on CISA KEV; fixes in every branch, no workaround
items.summary: Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-28 fixes CVE-2026-76418, a logic error in the remote access SSL VPN of Secure Firewall ASA and Secure FTD that lets an unauthenticated attacker reload the device with a crafted connection request when a tunnel group uses secondary authentication, and says Cisco's PSIRT became aware of active exploitation in October 2026; CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-29. Cisco names no actor, offers no workaround and lists first fixed releases for every ASA and FTD branch.

actions: In every Entra tenant you or your MSP administer, disable without deleting the seven ConnectWise application identities that ConnectWise lists by client ID (Cloud Backup is 506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae; the other six are in ConnectWise's advisory), dormant connections included, and keep them disabled, because ConnectWise's restoration of 2026-10-28 has partners consent a new application, “ConnectWise Cloud Backup for M365”, in each tenant, so take its details only from the instructions on ConnectWise's Trust Center; where Graph activity logs were enabled, review them for these apps until at least 90 minutes after you disabled them, because a token issued before the disable stays valid for up to 90 minutes, and preserve the sign-in and audit logs promptly without delaying containment, because Entra ID Free keeps only 7 days.
In the same tenants list the apps owned by the ConnectWise tenant (ID 3f9cd7a0-127a-4ed4-bf06-2f830d5616b7), and disable each that you do not use or cannot verify as safe.

In the same tenants review every enterprise application and app registration, MSP management and security tools first but none skipped (Huntress saw the secrets planted on apparently random applications, in one tenant on some of the least privileged ones), for client secrets, certificates and federated credentials added since 2026-10-13 and remove any you did not create; also check the directory roles, owners and consent grants held by ConnectWise and SkyKick service principals, Conditional Access exclusions for them, and mailbox forwarding, inbox and transport rules and delegated access, because disabling the vendor applications does not remove access planted through them.
items.headline: ConnectWise SkyKick app credential used in 162+ Microsoft 365 tenants; disabling it does not undo planted access
items.summary: ConnectWise says it identified unauthorized access to application identities of its Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) service; Huntress and Todyl report that from 15 October the app's credential was used to obtain app-only Microsoft Graph tokens in customer Microsoft 365 tenants; Huntress alone confirmed unauthorized sign-ins in 162 tenants by 16 October and saw ConnectWise Cloud Management apps assign themselves directory roles in about 50 tenants and, in two tenants, a scripted Global Administrator self-grant followed by new client secrets planted on apparently random applications. ConnectWise disabled seven application identities and suspended the service on 17 October, but says disabling does not reverse changes already made in a tenant, so every tenant that ever consented a ConnectWise or SkyKick app needs the apps disabled and its application credentials, directory roles and consents reviewed. Microsoft assesses that the China-state aligned actor Storm-0940 is behind it, using the ARTEX agentic-AI framework, and says it attempted sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants; how the credential was obtained and what data was read are not public.

items.headline: Talos: UAT-11473 implants KeyDrift in Cisco SD-WAN controllers through CVE-2026-20127 to collect data-plane keys
items.summary: Cisco Talos reports that a cluster it calls UAT-11473 exploited CVE-2026-20127, the peering authentication bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, Manager and Validator (CVSS 10.0, fixed releases since February 2026, no workaround), and then ran the KeyDrift implant inside the controller's control-plane process to collect session metadata and what Talos assesses to be data-plane IPsec keys. Cisco's advisory, revised on 2026-10-28 to link Talos's post, says it is aware of limited exploitation, and Talos assesses with high confidence that the operating infrastructure overlaps considerably with Volt Typhoon's Silent Train network.

items.headline: Apple's exploited CoreGraphics zero-day is now fixed for iPhone XS, XS Max, XR and iPad 7th generation (iOS 18.7.11)
items.summary: Apple's 2026-09-28 updates (iOS and iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1, macOS Sequoia 15.8.1) fix CVE-2026-86950, a CoreGraphics out-of-bounds write that can run arbitrary code when a crafted file is processed, and iOS and iPadOS 18.7.11 of 2026-10-26 carry the fix for iPhone XS, XS Max, XR and iPad 7th generation, which the 26.7.1 notes do not list. Apple says it may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals on versions of iOS before iOS 27, CISA added it to the KEV catalog on 2026-09-29, and no source states how the file is delivered. Since 2026-09-30 a public proof of concept crashes unpatched devices with a crafted PDF font.

actions: Upgrade every self-hosted Metabase to at least 0.58.24 / 0.59.21 / 0.60.17 / 0.61.11 / 0.62.9 / 0.63.5, then, for any instance that was reachable and unpatched during the exploitation window, revoke all active sessions by clearing the core_session table, delete unrecognised API keys, and rotate the credentials for every connected database and warehouse, not just the Metabase admin credentials, because the upgrade does not invalidate what was already retrieved.

Search Metabase application or reverse-proxy ingress logs across the entire pre-upgrade exposure window for a POST to /api/session/reset_password returning HTTP 400 immediately followed by a GET to /api/user/current returning HTTP 200 from the same source; Metabase states that sequence indicates the instance was likely compromised.

items.headline: Metabase Cloud was breached through its own 0-day; self-hosted instances stay vulnerable until manually upgraded
items.summary: Metabase disclosed on 2026-08-06 that its Metabase Cloud platform was attacked through a previously unknown vulnerability in versions 1.58 and above: an unauthenticated attacker injects arbitrary SQL against the application database and obtains administrator access to the instance, from which they can rewrite configuration, steal the stored credentials for every connected database and export the data those connections reach. The only interim workaround the vendor offers is to block the /api/session/reset_password endpoint, which is also where its published attack pattern runs. Cloud instances were patched by the vendor; self-hosted deployments stay vulnerable until manually upgraded to 0.58.24, 0.59.21, 0.60.17, 0.61.11, 0.62.9 or 0.63.5. Laptop maker Framework and form builder Tally confirmed customer data was taken from instances accessed on 2026-08-03. The flaw had no CVE identifier at disclosure; it is now tracked as CVE-2026-72898, which CISA added to its KEV catalog on 2026-08-11. VenariX now tracks fifteen publicly confirmed downstream incidents and ties two of them, at Statista and Dodo Payments, to the Dire Wolf extortion group working against self-hosted instances.

actions: On every WordPress site your organisation, its web agencies or its hosting suppliers run with UpdraftPlus, free or premium, including old municipal, campaign and project sites, check for an UpdraftCentral key (wp option get updraft_central_localkeys, or Settings > UpdraftPlus Backups > Advanced Tools > UpdraftCentral) and delete every key even if nobody remembers using UpdraftCentral, then update to 1.26.13 or 2.26.13 or later; deleting a key stops remote management only, and backups keep working.

On any site where a plugin, must-use plugin or Editor account holding manage_options appears that nobody created, delete the UpdraftCentral key first, then restore the site from a backup taken before 17 October, rotate every administrator and UpdraftCentral password, the teamupdraft.com account password (which UpdraftPlus Premium can leave stored in the site database and its backups) and end all sessions.
items.headline: Stolen UpdraftCentral keys install backdoor plugins on WordPress sites; the plugin update alone does not evict them
items.summary: TeamUpdraft, the vendor of the UpdraftPlus backup plugin, says unauthorised access to teamupdraft.com on 17 and 18 October probably exposed its customer database, including UpdraftCentral connection keys, and Patchstack and Nethemba report an attacker using those keys to install backdoor plugins on connected WordPress sites, which Patchstack's telemetry dates from 2026-10-18 15:32 (it gives no time zone), and that create hidden administrators. It is not a flaw in UpdraftPlus: the plugin obeys commands signed with a valid key, a key exists on many sites that never used the service because connecting a teamupdraft.com account ticks the option by default, and the update disconnects only connections made before 13:07 BST (12:07 UTC) on 18 October, so keys created later that day have to be deleted by hand. TeamUpdraft says the attacker used a compromised key to enter its own site, and Nethemba saw the stolen keys used again on 2026-10-21, after 1.26.13 shipped.

actions: Patch every PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal and gateway to the fixed build in Palo Alto's advisory for its minor release (users then re-authenticate once, because the fixed firewall regenerates the override cookie), or until then disable Authentication Override or give the cookies a certificate that no other feature uses.

On every GlobalProtect gateway that was internet-reachable and unpatched at any time since 2026-05-17, treat the network behind it as a ransomware compromise-assessment target: review VPN sessions that authenticated by cookie from unexpected sources, check Windows hosts for the artifacts Arctic Wolf describes (a ransomware payload staged under C:\\PerfLogs, a PsExec service, an LSASS dump written through comsvcs.dll to an .odt file, an ntdsutil media copy of the Active Directory database, and cleared event logs), and extend the assessment to the virtualization and backup tier: vCenter and ESXi audit logs for a changed execInstalledOnly setting and for access to a domain controller's virtual disk, and the Veeam backup server, because Unit 42 describes one intrusion that pivoted from the gateway to vCenter and dumped domain credentials offline, which in-guest EDR does not see.

cves.affected: PAN-OS 12.1, 11.2, 11.1 and 10.2 below the fixed builds, with a GlobalProtect portal or gateway where authentication override cookies are enabled and a specific certificate configuration exists; Prisma Access 11.2 and 10.2 below the fixed builds

items.headline: Qilin and Inc ransomware exploit the GlobalProtect bypass; one intrusion pivoted to vCenter and ESXi past in-guest EDR
items.summary: CVE-2026-0257 is a pre-auth VPN authentication bypass in PAN-OS GlobalProtect (CISA KEV; Palo Alto reports limited exploit attempts, and Rapid7 and Unit 42 report successful exploitation): an attacker forges valid auth-override cookies by re-using the GlobalProtect certificate shared with the HTTPS service, with no credentials. CISA's KEV catalog (version 2026.10.04) marks it as used in known ransomware campaigns, and Arctic Wolf's report of 2026-07-20 describes June 2026 intrusions in which Qilin ransomware deployment began with this bypass. Unit 42 now names Qilin and Inc as exploiting it and describes one intrusion that pivoted from the VPN gateway to vCenter and ESXi and stole domain credentials offline from a domain controller's virtual disk, which in-guest EDR does not see. Patch or disable auth-override cookies, and treat a gateway that was exposed and unpatched as a compromise-assessment target that includes the virtualization and backup tier.

actions: List every monitoring server, script, scheduled task and connection manager that stores an ESXi, vCenter or Proxmox root password, replace each with a least-privilege monitoring account, and rotate the root passwords that were stored or reused across hosts.
items.headline: Kaspersky: ESXi and Proxmox ransomware ran on a monitoring server's root password and admin notes, no VM escape
items.summary: Kaspersky's Global Emergency Response Team describes two ransomware cases in virtualised estates. In the BlackNevas case a PRTG Network Monitor held ESXi root access and the same root password was reused across hosts, so the attacker connected over SSH, disabled the execInstalledOnly policy with esxcli, ran the encryptor and deleted logs; in the case attributed to The Gentlemen the actor found Proxmox root credentials in plaintext notes on an administrator workstation and used the VNC web socket to encrypt the cluster. Kaspersky stresses that no VM escape was needed.

items.headline: Brotli flaw hits Desigo CC, Industrial Edge and Mitel; Cisco lists Duo; Mitel and Common Configurator fixes pending
items.summary: Between 2026-10-27 and 2026-11-06 Siemens, Mitel and Cisco listed affected products in advisories that cover the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497: Siemens names Desigo CC V8 and V9 (remedy: the latest .NET security updates) and Industrial Edge, where Common Configurator has no fix; Mitel names MiVoice Business and five OpenScape products with updates planned and workaround articles for three; Cisco's combined advisory lists Duo Network Gateway (3.4.2) and RoomOS among its products with fixes, a longer list of which is dated up to 2027, without saying which of its CVEs each fix addresses. Cisco says it is not aware of malicious use against any Cisco product, and CISA lists the flaw as exploited.

items.summary: OpenSSH Portable 10.6p2 of 2026-11-05 works around CVE-2026-123158, a password-authentication bypass on Linux systems that use musl libc and run sshd without PAM, Alpine's default OpenSSH server and OpenWrt among them: a password of 257 to 1,024 bytes logs in to an account whose password field is *. NCSC Switzerland published an advisory the same day and rates exploitation unknown; Alpine shipped fixed packages for every branch back to 3.16. Previdian's page, as read on 2026-11-07, reports 15 exploitation attempts from 10 addresses since 2026-11-06 and, according to The Hacker News, a successful root login on an Alpine honeypot; CISA does not list the flaw.

actions: In every Okta org that allows self-service registration, review the accounts created since 2026-10-13 and every Okta Verify enrollment on them, and remove self-created accounts that nobody provisioned.
items.headline: Microsoft: Storm-0940 runs ARTEX at machine speed; Mandiant now sees agent frameworks in incident-response cases
items.summary: Microsoft reports that since at least September 2026 Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, has used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework, to automate scanning, password spraying and OAuth-application abuse against hundreds of organizations across many industries including government, reaching privileged cloud access in under three hours in several cases; Expel saw the same infrastructure create its own accounts through Okta self-service registration. Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report on 2026-10-31 that since late August they have seen ARTEX, PentAGI and CAIRN operated in incident-response cases, with ARTEX adopted by extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters whose victims include US government organizations, and that the original ARTEX repository was taken down in October while forks keep it in circulation. CrowdStrike and Recorded Future document another actor using the framework, and Seoul police referred a criminal group's leader to prosecutors on 2026-10-23 for extorting 38 of more than 90 organizations, with the same framework according to BleepingComputer. Microsoft adds on 2026-11-06 another cluster, the Cambodia-based, financially motivated Storm-3358 targeting financial organisations, and Check Point reads ten exposed operator consoles that show near-autonomous, opportunistic ARTEX campaigns.

actions: Upgrade every FreeSWITCH to 1.11.3, or until then set enable-chat=false on every SIP profile that does not need inbound SIP chat and remove directory users that have no password; on an instance that SIP peers could reach, rotate the SIP trunk and directory credentials stored in its configuration, because the advisory lists disclosure of configuration and credentials as an impact and says exploitation has been observed.

cves.fixed: FreeSWITCH 1.11.3, which adds a per-profile enable-chat-api-proto parameter that is off unless set

items.headline: FreeSWITCH: one SIP MESSAGE runs API commands, vendor says exploited; fixed in 1.11.3
items.summary: SignalWire's advisory of 2026-10-28 describes CVE-2026-116779 (CVSS 3.1 9.8): an inbound SIP MESSAGE to a FreeSWITCH SIP profile selects the api chat proto and runs FreeSWITCH API commands with the privileges of the FreeSWITCH process, in the default configuration of 1.11.2 and earlier, and the advisory states that exploitation of this path has been observed in the wild. BSI CERT-Bund relayed it as a critical advisory on 2026-11-05; no source names an actor or victim, and the exploitation claim is the vendor's alone.

items.summary: The Linux kernel CVE team published CVE-2026-98432 on 2026-10-15, a use-after-free in the IPv4 TCP connection setup path that dates to Linux 4.4 and is reached by a SYN packet carrying IP options; the CNA scores it CVSS 9.8. items.headline: SpecterOps: iSCSI Target Server without CHAP lets a host that knows the target and initiator names read shared disks
items.summary: SpecterOps (2026-11-04) shows that a Windows iSCSI Target Server configured as a common cluster guide describes, with the optional CHAP step skipped, accepts a login from any host that knows the target host, the target name and an authorised initiator name, and the post says the host and the names can be found. The attacker then reads the shared disk below file-system permissions; where it holds a Hyper-V domain controller's virtual disk, the directory database and local credential stores are exposed. CHAP, network segmentation and volume encryption are the levers.

items.summary: OPSSHIELD's disclosure of 2026-11-03 says an attacker registered as a customer on its billing portal and ran commands on the billing and licensing server, through crafted requests to the portal's callback pages (the vendor's logs do not record the exact request that gave access), took the keys used to publish updates and shipped a fake cPGuard update for about 70 minutes on 2026-11-02 (02:08 to 03:20 UTC). items.headline: GhostAction: fake security workflows now harvest whole git histories; rotating Actions secrets is not enough
items.summary: StepSecurity and Socket report that on 2026-10-08 the GhostAction campaign used the GitHub credentials of two open-source maintainers to commit a workflow disguised as a security audit straight to the default branch of 345 to 346 repositories, including one of an Uber-owned organisation, and that the workflow now sends the credentials found in the working tree and in the entire git history, besides the named Actions secrets, to a hardcoded address over plain HTTP. GitGuardian's own data puts the wave of 8 to 12 October at more than 30,000 repositories reached through about 1,900 compromised GitHub accounts, and says GitHub has prevented the workflow from running since 9 October. Between 13 and 21 October the operator pushed at least 72,026 further commits, mostly from accounts whose tokens were already used on 8 October, including a stealer disguised as a font file that a hidden VS Code task runs on developer machines, outside GitHub's workflow hold, and a cron job that survives cleaning the repository.

items.headline: Eight eMudhra CA keys were guessable; Windows drops seven certificates, and Java, Python, Go and GitLab need updates
items.summary: On 2026-10-17 a researcher reported that the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates had been generated with too little randomness, so anyone could recover them and forge trusted HTTPS certificates for any site. Firefox, Chrome, Apple and Microsoft platforms block the intermediates and eMudhra revoked them; Microsoft went further on 2026-10-26 and removed seven eMudhra-hierarchy certificates from the Windows trust list, and from the Edge trust list on 2026-10-27. Software that keeps its own trust store or does not check revocation stays exposed until updated: Go fixed it in 1.27.3 and 1.26.10 as CVE-2026-111943, GitLab in its releases of 2026-10-29, Python added a built-in denylist as CVE-2026-115557, and Java needs the second update of 2026-10-24 (CVE-2026-114820, CVSS 3.1 9.1) even on a runtime updated in the past few days. Chrome's removal of the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root was due on 2026-10-27; Cisco's advisory dates its ISE fixes to December 2026 and April 2027, and no exploitation is reported.

items.headline: Microsoft: Teams help-desk vishing into Quick Assist ended in AD CS certificates for privileged accounts and a DC
items.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes two human-operated intrusions, not attributed to any actor, in which an external Teams contact impersonating help-desk staff got a user to open Quick Assist, after which the operator staged a portable runtime and used Active Directory Certificate Services to reach privileged identities: a template open to ESC1 issued certificates for privileged accounts and DCSync followed within seconds, and in the second case PetitPotam was relayed to AD CS Web Enrollment (ESC8) for a certificate for a domain controller account. An issued certificate stays valid after a password reset or a reimage of the first workstation, and in the first case one privileged account excluded from automated containment stayed usable and was used to copy data to an external SFTP destination.

items.headline: Cursor marketplace served a trojanised Claude Code extension for 11 hours; uninstalling leaves the SSH backdoor
items.summary: Between about 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29 the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace served a modified copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for macOS and Windows, that appends an attacker's SSH key to authorized_keys, tries to enable SSH and open a reverse tunnel, and installs persistence that outlives the extension. Coding errors made the SSH step fail on most standard-user hosts, so Cursor and Sophos say the attacker could not log in there, but the key, the persistence and a host report were still written. Anthropic told Microsoft its systems were not compromised, and no source says how the attacker published under Anthropic's name.

items.headline: SafeDep and JFrog: the testmetest npm worm now runs on import, so --ignore-scripts does not stop it; 42 repos armed
items.summary: SafeDep and JFrog describe an npm worm, tracked as testmetest, whose newest builds start when an application imports the package, so installing with --ignore-scripts does not stop it. It steals SSH, registry, cloud, CI and AI-tool credentials, publishes new patch versions of the victim's own packages, and wipes the home directory when the stolen GitHub token is revoked. SafeDep counts 19 packages from one operator between 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-27; JFrog found 42 armed GitHub repositories of 11 legitimate owners; neither lab names an actor.

items.headline: Huntress: phished MDM enrolments push ScreenConnect back after removal; the RMM is not the root of the intrusion
items.summary: Huntress reports several recent incidents in which phishing victims ended up with an MDM client from Hexnode or Rippling followed by an unauthorised ScreenConnect agent. Huntress says the products are not at fault and that removing the RMM does not remove the management architecture behind it.

items.headline: LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI and in the official images stole cloud and AI credentials; removing the package does not stop it
items.summary: On 2026-10-21 LiteLLM 1.107.0, the open-source LLM gateway, shipped with malicious Python startup files in all seven PyPI wheels (live 11:39 to 13:23 UTC) and in the official GHCR and Docker Hub images behind the v1.107.0, latest, main-latest and main-stable tags (11:46 to 14:20 UTC); they run a credential stealer at every Python start and start a background loader that could execute code fetched from an attacker-chosen host, though Socket saw its pointer empty at 13:01 UTC. The maintainers' root-cause post of 2026-10-23 says a master key committed to a public repository on 2026-05-27 and never revoked gave the attacker, from 2026-10-10, a GitHub organization owner's CLI token, with which it stole two maintainers' tokens and, on 2026-10-21, overrode branch protection to build the release from a look-alike repository; Socket independently found secret-stealing workflows running on 2026-10-10. Wiz saw stolen AWS instance-role credentials tested about 4.5 hours after exfiltration; PyPI and the registries removed the release the same day and the maintainers say to pin 1.106.2 or an explicit earlier version.

actions: Confirm that every domain controller has the cumulative update of 2026-10-13 and every Windows server the September 2026 one for its Windows release (SpecterOps names KB5126646, the October update for Windows Server 2025, and KB5122882, the September update for Windows Server 2022; other releases have their own packages), then list the computer accounts whose msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity or msDS-KeyCredentialLink holds a value nobody set, because patching does not remove what a relay already wrote.
items.headline: Required LDAP and SMB signing did not stop NTLM relay: a re-authenticated session kept the attacker's key
items.summary: SpecterOps (LDAP, 2026-10-23) and Blackfield (SMB, 2026-10-21) independently show that a domain controller or file server that requires signing still accepts a relayed NTLM authentication when the attacker first opens a signed session of its own and then re-authenticates it as the victim, so the session keeps a signing key the attacker knows. Microsoft fixed the SMB variant in September 2026 and the LDAP variant in the 2026-10-13 cumulative update; SpecterOps reports no reply to its report and Blackfield found no CVE for the SMB change; public tooling exists and neither researcher reports use in attacks.

items.headline: SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier: unauthenticated file read, no fix will ship; replace with NSM
items.summary: SonicWall's advisory SNWLID-2026-0019 of 2026-11-03 says an unauthenticated attacker with network access to SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier may read internal GMS files (CVE-2026-109593, CVSS 3.1 9.1), with a post-authentication SQL injection beside it (CVE-2026-109594, 6.8). The product reached end of support on 2026-09-30, so SonicWall releases no fix, names no workaround and urges migration to Network Security Manager; the advisory says nothing about exploitation.
